title: Coding differently in 4D V12
author: Christophe Keromen, Cabinet de Consultants CKTI
featured_technology: Method comments and code editor help tips
Code folding, method Explorer, and 'Goto Definition'

historical_commentary.text: Most of the code-editor productivity techniques here (structured comments, help tips, folding, ASSERT, Goto Definition, renaming, hyperlinked comments) operate within 4D's classic binary Design Mode method editor and are still functionally present and useful in current 4D, so they remain largely still relevant as coding hygiene practices. However, since methods now live as plain text files under Project mode, some workflow specifics (e.g., navigating the binary Explorer, component-private-method highlighting tied to old component packaging) are dated, and text-based version control/diffing now offers additional refactoring safety nets that did not exist in 2011.
related_updates: Project mode (text-based .4DProject structure/methods, introduced 4D v17, 2018) changes how code is organized, versioned, and diffed compared to binary Design Mode
4D language classes (introduced v18/v19) offer additional modern code-organization patterns beyond the method-level tips described here
